about: A new stall in the school canteen

lines.text: Our school canteen has had the same six stalls for as long as anyone remembers.
Last term, however, a seventh stall open beside the drinks counter, and it
lines.note: Tense: 'last term' is in the past, so it is 'opened'.

lines.text: quickly became the most popular one. The stall sells only three dish: noodle soup,
fried rice and a vegetable wrap. The owner, Mdm Lee, cook everything herself
lines.note: Agreement: 'the owner' is one person, so it is 'cooks'.

lines.text: and arrives at six every morning to prepare the ingredients. Her prices are low,
and she always gives an extra spoonful to students who look hungry. During recess,
the queue for her stall are longer than all the other queues put together.
lines.note: Agreement: 'the queue' is one thing, so it is 'is'.

lines.text: Some students even skip their snack so that they can buy a early lunch
lines.note: Article: 'early' starts with a vowel sound, so it is 'an early lunch'.

lines.text: from her. Mdm Lee remembers the names of almost every student, and she greets them warm
lines.note: Word form: 'greets' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'warmly'.

lines.text: each day. Last week, two teacher joined the queue for the first time.
They ordered the noodle soup and finish every drop before the bell rang.
lines.note: Tense: 'ordered … and finished' — both verbs are in the past.

lines.text: Mdm Lee only smiled and said that good food needs no advertisement.
